chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from al-Abbas ibn Amir who said:

I asked him about a man who had been bequeathed to with a bequest, then he died before taking possession of it and did not leave any offspring. He said: 'Seek out an inheritor or a guardian for him, and hand it over to him.'

I said: 'So if I do not know a guardian for him?' He said: 'Strive to the best of your ability to find a guardian for him; and if you still cannot find one, and God — Mighty and Majestic — knows the earnest striving from you, then give it in charity.'

key_terms.الْجِدّ: Earnest striving, diligence — sincere effort made in fulfilling one's obligations
key_terms.تَصَدَّقَ: To give in charity (sadaqa) — the prescribed final recourse when no rightful claimant is found
key_terms.عَقِب: Offspring, descendants — those who follow in lineage
key_terms.مَوْلَى: Patron/guardian — a freed slave, client, or tribal protector; in this context, one with a custodial relationship
key_terms.وَارِث: Inheritor — one who receives property by right of inheritance
key_terms.وَصِيَّة: Bequest — property designated for a specific recipient in a will
key_terms.وَلِيّ: Guardian/custodian — the legal guardian or protector of a person or estate

ai.seo_question: What happens to a bequest if the beneficiary dies before taking possession with no heirs in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from one of the Imams (peace be upon them) regarding the disposition of a bequest whose designated beneficiary died without leaving heirs before taking possession. The Imam instructs a three-stage resolution: first, search for a blood inheritor or a patron-guardian; second, if none is found despite diligent effort, give the property as charity. The hadith emphasizes that sincere effort (al-jidd) is itself a criterion — God's knowledge of one's genuine striving legitimizes the final charitable disposition, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential principle that righteous intent and diligent effort are prerequisites for lawful resolution in ambiguous inheritance cases.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ayoub Bin Nuh, from Al Abbas Bin Aamir who said,

‘I asked the Imam<sup>asws</sup> about a man who had been bequeathed to, so he (the beneficiary) died before taking possession, and did not leave any offspring. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Seek out his inheritors, or a guardian, so hand it over to him’.

I said, ‘So if I do not know who is guardian it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Strive over it in accordance to your ability, for his guardian, so if you still cannot find him, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Knows the striving from you, so give it in charity’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ayyub ibn Nuh from al-‘Abbas ibn ’Amir who has narrated the following: “I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of man in whose favor a will is made but he dies before taking possession and has not left any heirs.
He (the Imam) said, ‘You must search for his heirs or master then give it to him.’

I then asked, ‘What happens if I cannot find any guardian for him?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Try to find out his guardian and if you cannot find, and Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, knows your effort, then give it in charity on his behalf.’”
